items.title: 'Corruption behind it': The Trump-Kushner mega-deal that has left a nation angry
items.description: Albania's coastline has become a hotspot for cheap European summer sojourns but as Ivanka Trump claims her Christopher Columbus moment, locals are adamant that their island is not for sale.

items.title: Trump holds off on new strikes against Iran amid emerging 'deal'
items.description: Donald Trump says the US will hold off on fresh strikes against Iran, as Middle East allies have agreed to parameters of a deal to end the war.

items.title: Australia records biggest-ever surge in EV sales
items.description: Nearly one in every two new vehicles sold was either electric or hybrid across April, May and June.

items.title: Eighteen days in a Japanese police cell killed our daughter, family says
items.description: A 16-year-old girl's family alleges she was so traumatised by her time in a police cell, it killed her. Her case is now the focus of court action alleging she was a victim of Japan's "hostage justice" system.

items.title: Five dead, 41 missing after Indonesian ferry catches fire
items.description: Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry with 271 people on board caught fire while at sea, search and rescue officials say.

items.title: Garma land council announcement sparks concern in region
items.description: A key clan elder on the Gove Peninsula has voiced his frustration, confusion and concern over a bold plan to create a new Aboriginal land council in his region.

items.title: Prices to jump at the bowser as fuel excise cut ends tonight
items.description: The price of unleaded and diesel will climb in the next week as the government's fuel excise cut officially ends. But experts say prices won't go as high as they did due to increased supply.

items.title: Fears shared on Australia reaching bleak milestone in spread of H5 bird flu
items.description: There are fears Australia has reached a bleak milestone in the spread of H5 bird flu, following the discovery of a large group of dead and sick birds off South Australia's coast on Friday.

items.title: 'We'll kill you': Sandilands says he received threats in Stefanovic interview
items.description: In an interview with former Nine Today presenter, Karl Stefanovic, released on YouTube, Sandilands said threatening letters had been left at his office.

items.title: Live: Aussie cyclist 'proud not to spew' after gruelling gold-medal run
items.description: Australia's cyclists will look to close their incredibly successful Commonwealth Games with another swag of medals, before the closing ceremony brings the action in Glasgow to a close. Follow live.

items.title: Eagles star in tears after loss, Crows into top four after downing Dons
items.description: Willem Duursma breaks down after West Coast's loss to Richmond at the MCG as Adelaide ends round 21 inside the top four.

items.title: 'Rubbish' costs Rabbitohs as Hynes chases NRL record, Eels beat Tigers
items.description: South Sydney coach Wayne Bennett says "rubbish" from his team continues to cost them chances to win games, as the Rabbitohs are beaten by the Cronulla Sharks.

items.title: Grandfather and grandson pedal 5,300km from Broome to Bowral for MND
items.description: Bob Montgomery, 82, and his grandson Tom Malcolm, 18, have completed an epic cross-country cycling journey to raise money for research into motor neurone disease.

items.title: UTI led to Sydney woman's death three days after giving birth
items.description: Gia Lam gave birth to her son and was dead three days later. A coronial inquest found her death was preventable. Her family are now breaking their silence.

items.title: Love story: Adding three adoptive children was beautiful chaos
items.description: Anna and Mark Dombkins say their love for one another and helping others led them to move overseas to adopt.

items.title: From playing on a rock to rocking out — the 'steep rise' of Wild Honey
items.description: The grandsons of Yothu Yindi's lead singer have ambitions to take their band Wild Honey from Garma to the MCG and beyond.

items.title: Annabel Crabb's rich chocolate cake with a surprising ingredient
items.description: This moist, dark cake has an almost earthy richness and is perfect for those who don't love their desserts super sweet.

items.title: 'What's happened to me?': Bearing witness as my nan faced dementia
items.description: The woman who once chased down a donkey to save her granddaughter would one day need saving herself — and teach me a lesson about love.

items.title: Record-breaking Premier League move looms for Socceroo
items.description: Lucas Herrington is on the verge of a move to a Premier League club that would be the most expensive transfer for an Australian player.

items.title: Candles light up night to honour Melbourne mother Brooke Stephens
items.description: Hundreds gather at a park in Clyde North, one week after a local woman was allegedly murdered in her home.

items.title: Eight alleged offenders who cut off ankle bracelets spark police manhunt
items.description: The WA Police Union say six police officers were required to hunt each person who took off the device, meaning 48 officers were diverted from their usual duties this weekend.

items.title: Victoria Park masterplan for Brisbane 2032 unveiled
items.description: The draft plan includes Brisbane Stadium, the National Aquatic Centre at Centenary Pool, upgrades to Brisbane Showgrounds and "expanded" parklands and public spaces.

items.title: To prove how easy it is to buy unregulated peptides the ABC organised a deal
items.description: The injectable drugs have not been approved for use in Australia but are advertised widely on social media.

items.title: Trump's new respect for Zelenskyy highlights Netanyahu's problem
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy must have felt a little triggered walking into the Oval Office this week. But Donald Trump's public anger is now often directed at another at-war ally.

items.title: The US may have reached 'turning point' in school shooting punishments
items.description: For the third time in US history, a parent has been held criminally responsible for the murderous actions of their child. Legal experts have suggested it marks a turning point for American prosecutors.
